text:
maya: Ran a quick Nsight Systems sweep on the rtx-dedicated pool with the short-chat workload (2k steps). Attached the timeline and a CSV export of kernel costs. Initial quick read: attention_dot_prod and shuffle_gemm are dominating total GPU time; KV-cache lookup has very high invocation count but low avg time. Also noticed periodic SM utilization drops coinciding with large KV cache misses.

jon: can you paste the top kernels by self-time here? and SM util for attention_dot_prod?

maya: Pasting the top-5 by cumulative self time from the export (nsys sample):

```
#kernel,total_ms,invocations,avg_ms,sm_util,occupancy
attention_dot_prod,482.3,240,2.0096,78%,0.63
shuffle_gemm,310.9,120,2.5908,92%,0.88
kv_cache_lookup,95.4,840,0.1136,34%,0.21
softmax_fwd,80.6,240,0.3358,60%,0.45
layernorm_fwd,45.1,240,0.1879,20%,0.12
```

maya: timeline quick notes: attention_dot_prod shows long kernels with high active SMs but frequent stalls waiting on global loads when sequence>2048. shuffle_gemm appears extremely compute-bound (high SM util & occ), likely GEMM layout mismatch causing excessive shared mem bank conflicts on our kernel. KV cache lookups are small but bursty; when a miss happens we see a cascade of attention kernels redoing work.

rico: interesting. For attention_dot_prod, what kernel variant are we running? fused_multi_head from our 'fam' path or the fallback 'attn_basic'?

maya: it's currently using attn_basic for the GPT-medium variant due to minor numerics mismatch in fused_multi_head. So cost reflects fallback.

jon: that explains it. Fused kernel typically halves global load stalls. Any perf regressions compared to last week's baseline?

maya: Yes—compared to baseline (1768000000 nsight run), attention time increased ~22% on identical workload. I pulled nvtx ranges and the delta aligns with the revert we did to attn_basic in the model switch patch.

perf-bot: CI trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/nsys/1768507423/trace.nsight (artifact)
